Harvest of Cryptoole records (research/cryptoole/candidates.md) listed Paolo Rosson's gonzaga-1590 page (row FR1586-3) with 'Already here' left blank: the page was not matched to this folder, although it covers the same cipher and the fr. 4698 pages in Lasry's entry. Prior art missed.

Issue #708 (Brice Dudout) pointed to Rosson's folder gonzaga-1590 (pangoleen/cipher-readings; commits 3-4 Oct 2026 by his record): period decipherments of fr. 4698 ff. 30r-31r and f. 104r by Nevers's clerk in BnF fr. 4702 ff. 94r-95r and 97r-v, his editions and translations, a rebuilt word code (448 values in 14 lists) and symbol alphabet, a test on fr. 4696 (452 of 463 units, 97.6%). Read in a local clone; the GitHub API for his repository was not available, so push dates are not known.

Model checks of Rosson's folder (no person): tables/lists_v4.tsv holds 448 data rows in 14 lists; the fr. 4696 figure adds up (387 + 21 + 44 = 452 of 463); Gallica fr. 4702 f. 94r seen, a clear Italian decipherment in a clerk's hand, first lines matching his transcription; his edition of 21 Jan 1590 contains the run Lasry reads on f. 30v ('richiedermi ... prieghi'). Not checked: unit-by-unit alignments, symbol alphabet, shuffle test, whether Lasry's 24 nomenclature values are a subset of his lists, f. 104r against the clerk's text.

Recorded the period decipherments of fr. 4698 ff. 30r-31r and f. 104r (fr. 4702 ff. 94r-95r, 97r-v), as edited by Rosson, as a second reading of those pages next to Lasry's; nothing was deciphered or re-measured here (no cipher-words-only share).

texts.label: George Lasry's decipherment (report PDF, 24 Oct 2026)
texts.summary: Scipion de Gonzague to the Duke of Nevers, 1585-1589 (BnF fr. 4696), and a letter of 1590 by an unestablished writer (fr. 4698). Confidential warnings and cavalry arrangements: horses, payments, dispatches and service in war. The fr. 4698 fragment contains a request for an appeal or intercession, and the Paris letter of 16 February 1590 discusses friendship, the King of Spain and a request; most of both remains unread.
